overview_description.description: Tabadulat is a digital brokerage platform designed to provide Shariah-compliant investment opportunities. It enables users to trade over 60,000 halal-certified stocks across various global markets. The platform offers features such as fractional share investing, advanced analytics, and AI-powered insights, all while ensuring adherence to AAOIFI standards through supervision by independent scholars. Tabadulat emphasizes transparency with ultra-low trading fees starting from 0.25% and provides tools like a Zakat calculator and real-time compliance tracking. The service is currently in a pre-launch phase, inviting users to sign up for early access.​

about_short_description.short_description: Tabadulat is a Shariah-compliant brokerage platform offering access to global halal stocks with low trading fees.​

product.name: Tabadulat Trading Platform
product.description: A Shariah-compliant, execution-only brokerage platform for buying and selling screened investments across global markets through a mobile app or website.

product.name: Halal Stock Screening
product.description: A screening service that evaluates stocks against Shariah criteria covering business activities and financial ratios, with ongoing monitoring and compliance status updates.

product.name: Halal Stocks
product.description: Access to equities that pass Tabadulat’s Shariah screening, with trading, portfolio tracking, and market data through the Tabadulat platform.

product.name: Halal ETFs
product.description: Exchange-traded funds comprising Shariah-compliant assets, intended to provide diversified market exposure through a single listed investment.

product.name: Shariah-Compliant REITs
product.description: Access to Real Estate Investment Trusts that meet Shariah requirements, enabling investment exposure to income-producing real estate through listed securities.

product.name: Sukuk
product.description: Access to Shariah-compliant Sukuk instruments, which represent interests in assets or economic activities rather than conventional interest-bearing debt.
